# 百千印陀羅尼經

**ID:** T1369b
**Volume:** T21
**Category:** 密教部類
**Original Category:** 密教部
**Byline:** 唐 實叉難陀譯
**Dynasty:** 唐
**Date:** 695–704
**Juans:** 1
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T1369b

## Contributors
- 實叉難陀 (A001606)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A short Táng-period translation by [實叉難陀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AF%A6%E5%8F%89%E9%9B%A3%E9%99%80) Śikṣānanda (652–710), preserved as the **second recension** of the work also represented by [KR6j0599](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0599) (T1369a). The colophon here reads "唐于闐三藏實叉難陀譯" — the Táng/Khotanese form, suggesting that this version may post-date the formal end of the Wǔ-Zhōu period (705) or simply reflects a different colophon-tradition. The text is the same in substance but differs from [KR6j0599](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0599) in transcription detail (e.g. *bù-dì bù-dì bù-dì bù-dì* vs. *pú-tí pú-tí pú-tí pú-tí*) and in some minor framing elements.

**Abstract**

The frame is the same as [KR6j0599](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0599): Vulture-Peak with the *bhikṣu*-saṅgha and an immeasurable host of bodhisattvas; the dhāraṇī is to be received and held; before recitation one takes refuge in the *Jīnsè guǎngyán guāngmíngzhuàng fó* 金色廣顏光明幢佛 ("Golden-Form Broad-Visaged Light-Banner Buddha", here corresponding to the slightly different *miànmào guǎngdà dǐngchū zhēnjīn guāngmíngzhuàng* form of [KR6j0599](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0599)) and in Śākyamuni. The triple-dhāraṇī structure (root-heart-following-heart) is preserved. The closing rubric — "the merit of one *stūpa* with this dhāraṇī inside is the same as the merit of a hundred-thousand *stūpas*" — is identical.

The pair [KR6j0599](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0599)/[KR6j0600](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0600) is one of the rare cases where the Taishō preserves what are functionally two near-identical witnesses of one translation, distinguished principally by phonetic transcription convention. Their conjoint transmission illustrates Táng manuscript practice: the same translation could circulate in slightly divergent recensions through different copyist-traditions.
